parsed.notes: Lens B only: treatment/currency reviewed; support and quote fidelity were not independently assessed.

reasons: Lake identity is verified and matches the asserted Supreme Court case, date, docket, and citation set.
Lake treatment field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30, so the authority is disclosed as still live for its core holding.
residual_risks: No disclosed evidence verifies treatment after 2026-06-30.

defect.evidence_quote: Core holding (4A damages against federal officers) remains good law; the Court has declined to extend Bivens to new contexts (Ziglar v. Abbasi (2017); Egbert v. Boule (2022)).
defect.problem: Currency/treatment framing is too broad unless limited to the Bivens core context. The disclosed treatment says the core Fourth Amendment damages holding remains good law, but also says the Court has declined to extend Bivens to new contexts.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise to: In the Bivens core Fourth Amendment search-and-seizure context, a victim may recover money damages directly under the Constitution from federal officers acting under color of federal authority; the remedy is not a general federal-officer analog to section 1983 in new contexts.

reasons: No disclosed treatment overrules the core Bivens holding.
The disclosed scope note itself requires a limitation against new-context extension.
residual_risks: Support and quote fidelity were not reviewed under Lens B.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: State the Bivens-like Fourth Amendment context expressly and avoid implying full equivalence to section 1983.

reasons: For currency purposes, lake treatment lists the core Bivens holding as good_law.
The content page frames Bivens as foundational while disclosing sharp limits on extension to new contexts.
residual_risks: Home-role taxonomy is mostly outside Lens B; support fit was not independently audited.

reasons: Lake identity court_level is scotus and court is U.S. Supreme Court.
A Supreme Court decision is consistent with the asserted Binding — SCOTUS weight label.
residual_risks: Weight label does not itself communicate the disclosed new-context limitations.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep the weight label paired with the treatment scope note.

reasons: The content treatment fields match the lake treatment fields: good_law, as_of_content 1971-06-21, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, composite_basis migration-seed, varies_by_point false, and the same scope note.
Disclosed progeny edges are proposed and marked as mentioned; they do not disclose an audited overruling, supersession, or abrogation of Bivens itself.
The scope note expressly accounts for later limitation by Ziglar and Egbert while preserving the core holding.
residual_risks: Lake derivation flags audit_needed and cap_hit for some treatment searches, so the disclosed record supports the stated treatment as a lake judgment rather than a fresh exhaustive audit.
No disclosed evidence verifies events after 2026-06-30.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add that the good-law label applies only to the core Bivens context.
